profile.headline: SWE @ LPL Financial
profile.summary:
Hello! My name is Kai Williams. I am currently a Computer Science student at  San Diego State University with interests in software engineering, machine learning, AI, and data science. 

I enjoy building impactful technology, exploring intelligent systems, and solving real-world problems through software. My experience includes work in AI research, software development, and applied machine learning projects.

I’m always excited to connect with others in tech, learn from different experiences, and discuss opportunities in software engineering, AI/ML, and emerging technologies. Feel free to reach out!

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Team: Money Movement
• Develop C#/.NET backend services for production money movement across ACH, wire, and journal workflows.

• Develop an AI agent that interprets natural-language money movement requests and orchestrates multi-step financial transactions.

positions.title: GPU Research Assistant
positions.description:
Computer System Intelligence Lab - PI: Bryan Donyanavard
• Trained and optimized fused CNN architectures in C++/CUDA for MNIST classification, achieving 98% accuracy.

• Designed GPU-level optimizations including memory management and kernel coordination to improve throughput and reduce latency.

• Tuned SM-level resource utilization to maximize parallel execution efficiency on NVIDIA GPU architectures.

positions.title: AI Engineer Intern
positions.description:
Team: AI Labs
• Built a multi-threaded LLM-powered document processing pipeline to convert unstructured enterprise  documents into structured formats, reducing manual review time by 95%.

• Designed and deployed a RAG system using an S3-hosted knowledge base, improving response grounding with source-linked outputs, and integrated LLM-based tools into internal engineering workflows.

• Implemented a FAISS-based vector retrieval system (k-NN search) achieving 60.3% top-3 accuracy in customer feedback topic classification and improving retrieval efficiency for enterprise data.

positions.title: Data Privacy Research Assistant
positions.description:
Privacy and Anonymity Lab - PI: Joann Chen
• Applied differential privacy techniques to ad attribution datasets while preserving analytical utility across multiple privacy budgets .
 
• Implemented Laplace noise injection and user truncation methods, reducing attribution error and MSE by 90% while maintaining publisher-level accuracy.
 
• Contributed to research on privacy-preserving machine learning for advertising measurement systems and user data protection.

positions.title: Machine Learning Research Coordinator
positions.description:
AI4Business Lab - PI: Luwen Huangfu
• Co-authored and published peer-reviewed paper: “LLM-Driven Document Clustering: Improving Real-time Security Intelligence Extraction and Threat Analysis” at IEEE ISI 2025.
 
• Evaluated and enhanced the performance of K-means clustering and LDA algorithms, achieving a 14% improvement in clustering quality measured by key metrics consisting of Silhouette Score, Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI), Calinski-Harabasz Index (CHI), and Dunn Index.

• Conducted comprehensive first and second-round interviews to evaluate prospective candidates for the AI4Business Lab, accessing their proficiency in machine learning, coding, and soft skills.

positions.title: Machine Learning Research Assistant
positions.description:
AI4Business Lab - PI: Luwen Huangfu
• Applied Mixout regularization during LLM fine-tuning decreasing validation loss by 12% reducing overfitting and improving model generalization across diverse NLP datasets.
 
• Built a Python pipeline to extract and structure data from 100+ PDFs into JSON format, using TF-IDF and n-gram analysis to identify key patterns in large text corpora. 
 
• Conducted literature review on large language models and deep learning methods for NLP and information extraction systems

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
Team: FinOps
• Reduced CI/CD test execution time by 78% by implementing parallel execution using Python and YAML pipelines.
 
• Improved EC2 infrastructure compliance and cost efficiency by 20% through GP3 volume migration, instance resizing, and security group optimization.
 
• Increased engineering productivity by leveraging LLMs and RAG to generate contextual story and task guidance for new codebases.
positions.insights: Skills: Amazon Web Services (AWS) · Python (Programming Language) · Git · Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) · YAML

positions.title: STEM Instructor
positions.description:
• Implemented and delivered engaging programming, robotics, circuits, and mechanical systems workshops for diverse groups of students of 30+.

• Instructed students on the fundamentals of programming, covering essential topics including loops, recursion, and data structures.

• Guided students in completing 500+ coding, engineering, and science projects by offering individualized support and feedback.

honors.title: Liao-Huangfu "Light-House" Second-Stage Golden Award
honors.description:
The Liao-Huangfu "Light-House" Second-Stage Award, totaling approximately $17,500 across all award categories, recognizes outstanding research papers.

Alongside my co-authors, I submitted "Unveiling Language Mastery: Exploring Large Language Models for Academic Research," pioneering a cutting-edge two-step generative clustering approach utilizing LLMs. Our method introduced an advanced topic extractor for academic research winning the golden award, affirming our contribution to advancing research in the field.

publications.title: Large Language Model (LLM)-Driven Document Clustering: Improving Real-Time Security Intelligence Extraction and Threat Analysis
publications.publisher: IEEE International Conference on Intelligence and Security Informatics (ISI) · Dec 13, 2025
